title: Dirac's theorem on k vertices lying on a common cycle
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph, and let $k \ge 2$ be an integer such that $G$ is $k$-connected, that is, $k \le \kappa(G)$. Then for any set $T$ of exactly $k$ vertices of $G$, there is a cycle in $G$ whose vertices include every vertex of $T$.
hypotheses_covered: T is a set of exactly k vertices
replaced:
\emph{ (Dirac). }If \texttt{G} is \texttt{k}-connected with \texttt{k $\ge$ 2}, then any
\texttt{k} vertices of \texttt{G} are contained together in some cycle.*
